note: Team design rules for the Space Apps 2026 demo: planning thresholds chosen by the team from published lunar / Mars surface-operations practice, not NASA requirements. max_relief_m = allowed unevenness after removing the ground slope. Units: metres, degrees, seconds, m/s^2.

keepout_why.oman: Landing engines blast gravel outward. Keeping the camp clear of the pad protects it during every later landing and take-off.
keepout_why.moon: With no air to slow it, dust thrown by a landing engine flies for hundreds of metres at very high speed. Apollo 12 landed about 160 m from the Surveyor 3 probe and still pitted its surface. Camps on the Moon must sit well away from the pad, or behind a berm.
keepout_why.mars: Mars' thin air slows ejecta more than on the Moon, but a landing plume still throws gravel tens of metres. The camp stays outside that zone.

modules.name: Habitat
modules.role: Pressurised home for four crew, covered by a regolith berm that shields them from radiation.

why.slope: A habitat needs level ground: the floor, the airlock seal and the crew's bunks all assume a flat base, and an inflatable shell carries uneven loads on a slope.
why.relief: Bumps under the footprint must be graded flat before inflation; more than half a metre is too much regolith to move with the construction robot.

modules.name: Solar array
modules.role: Power for the base. A tall mast lifts the panels above the terrain's shadows.

why.sun: The panels must see the Sun. Near the lunar south pole the Sun skims only a few degrees above the horizon, so a small hill can shade a site for days; high ground is worth more than flat ground here.
why.distance: Power cables longer than about 160 m waste energy and are slow to lay across rough ground; keep the array close to the habitat.

modules.name: Comms mast
modules.role: Radio link to Earth (direct from the Moon, through an orbiting relay on Mars).

why.home: The dish needs a clear line of sight to Earth. From the lunar south pole Earth hangs low over the horizon, so any ridge in that direction cuts the link.
why.distance: The mast is wired to the habitat; within 200 m keeps the cable short and the mast inside the walking zone.

modules.name: Drill rig
modules.role: Moon: drills for water ice. Mars: cores layered sediments for signs of past life. Oman: cores the ophiolite, the project's analog rock.

why.shadow: Water ice survives only where the Sun never reaches: cold traps in permanent shadow, below about minus 160 °C. On the Moon the ice drill must stand in shadow.
why.distance: Crews and rovers service the drill from the habitat; within about 220 m keeps it a short drive away.

modules.name: Rover
modules.role: Pressurised rover parked by the habitat, ready for excursions.

why.slope: A parked rover needs gentle ground so it does not roll and can dock to the habitat's suit-ports.
why.distance: The rover garage must be a short walk from the airlock: within 60 m.

modules.name: Path marker
modules.role: Beacons that mark the safe walking route.

why.slope: Crews in suits should not walk on slopes steeper than about 25°.
